chapters.title: A voice looking back
chapters.summary: Kathy H., aged thirty-one, introduces herself as a carer with more than eleven years of experience. She takes pride in keeping donors calm, yet repeatedly qualifies her claims so that she will not sound boastful. Her references to donations, recovery centres and choosing donors initially receive little explanation: she speaks as though her listener already knows this world. Remembering a donor who wanted to borrow her happy childhood memories helps explain why Hailsham remains so important to her. Familiar buildings and landscapes still draw her back to it in her imagination. The narrative then moves to the school’s sports pavilion, where Kathy and her friends watch boys deliberately exclude Tommy from a football team, although he is a talented player. Laura imitates his expressions and the group finds excuses for the bullying. Kathy notices his treasured light-blue polo shirt and worries that his angry stamping will cover it in mud. She approaches him despite Ruth’s warning. Tommy accidentally hits her while flailing his arms, then becomes embarrassed. Their awkward encounter introduces both Kathy’s attentiveness and the pressure she feels from the watching group.
events: Kathy describes her work with donors.
Memories return her to Hailsham.
Tommy is excluded; Kathy approaches him.

analysis.detail: Kathy pauses to question whether she felt sympathy at the time.
analysis.effect: The older narrator distinguishes what she now understands from what her younger self may have felt. This uncertainty asks readers to evaluate her memory without assuming that every hesitation is a lie.
analysis.zh: retrospective narration 让成年判断与童年反应并存。她承认不确定，反而提醒读者：记忆是重建，不是录像；不能把 limited perspective 直接等同于故意撒谎。

analysis.detail: Professional words appear before the reader learns their full implications.
analysis.effect: The opening makes institutional routines sound familiar. Unease grows because the reader has to work out what those routines mean, experiencing the difference between hearing a term and understanding it.
analysis.zh: 作者先给词汇、后给含义。读者知道字面内容，却暂时不懂制度后果；这种阅读经验与小说中 knowledge 和 understanding 的距离相呼应。

analysis.detail: Kathy repeatedly notices Tommy’s treasured shirt.
analysis.effect: The shirt makes his vulnerability personal: what the crowd treats as a spectacle belongs to someone with ordinary attachments. Kathy’s attention begins to restore individuality to a boy reduced to a group joke.
analysis.zh: polo shirt 是具体的情感证据。群体只看见发脾气的笑柄，Kathy 却记得他珍惜的东西；这种细节把 Tommy 重新呈现为有感情的个人。

chapters.question: Why does Kathy focus on Tommy’s shirt rather than simply describing his tantrum?
chapters.answer: The shirt reveals an ordinary attachment that the watching group ignores. Her attention makes Tommy an individual and opens a small connection, while her embarrassment shows the limits of her independence from the group.
chapters.zh: 这一章先由31岁的 Kathy H. 介绍自己：她已经做了十一年多 carer，还要继续八个月。她为自己能让 donors 保持平静而自豪，却又不断补充、修正，怕听起来像在炫耀。作者没有立刻解释 donation 等词，而是让 Kathy 像对熟悉制度的人一样说话。随后，一个病重 donor 想把她的 Hailsham 回忆当成自己的童年，这说明记忆能够安慰人，也解释她为什么反复回到过去。叙述转到十二三岁时：女孩们在 sports pavilion 看男孩故意不选 Tommy 踢球。Tommy 明明球技很好，却受到集体排斥；Laura 模仿他的表情，其他人把责任推给他的脾气和缺乏创造力。Kathy 注意到他珍爱的浅蓝 polo shirt，担心被泥弄脏，于是走近提醒。他挥动手臂时意外碰到她的脸。重点不只是 Kathy 善良：她也曾旁观、受同伴眼光影响。这个不完全光彩的回忆让她显得复杂而真实。
chapters.titleZh: 回望过去的声音

orientation.en: Adult Kathy introduces her work, then moves back to Hailsham at twelve or thirteen. The chapter deliberately mixes the narrating present with remembered childhood.
orientation.zh: 先分清两个时间层：31岁的 Kathy 正在讲述；她回忆中的学生大约十二三岁。开头的 carer 工作与后面的校园事件不是同时发生。

chapters.summaryZh: 这一章先由31岁的 Kathy H. 介绍自己：她已经做了十一年多 carer，还要继续八个月。她为自己能让 donors 保持平静而自豪，却又不断补充、修正，怕听起来像在炫耀。作者没有立刻解释 donation 等词，而是让 Kathy 像对熟悉制度的人一样说话。随后，一个病重 donor 想把她的 Hailsham 回忆当成自己的童年，这说明记忆能够安慰人，也解释她为什么反复回到过去。叙述转到十二三岁时：女孩们在 sports pavilion 看男孩故意不选 Tommy 踢球。Tommy 明明球技很好，却受到集体排斥；Laura 模仿他的表情，其他人把责任推给他的脾气和缺乏创造力。Kathy 注意到他珍爱的浅蓝 polo shirt，担心被泥弄脏，于是走近提醒。他挥动手臂时意外碰到她的脸。重点不只是 Kathy 善良：她也曾旁观、受同伴眼光影响。这个不完全光彩的回忆让她显得复杂而真实。

scenes.title: A reassuring introduction with unsettling gaps
scenes.titleZh: 平静开场里的信息空缺
scenes.text: Kathy presents her job through competence, patience and professional recognition. She can choose some donors, and she anticipates other carers resenting this privilege. Because she does not explain the larger system, readers must notice the tension between her reassuring vocabulary and the references to repeated donations. Her concern with being judged also establishes a narrator who carefully manages how her account sounds.
scenes.zh: Kathy 先讲职业能力、耐心和成绩，使 carer 听起来很普通；但多次 donation、身体恢复等细节逐渐带来不安。她预想别人会嫉妒自己的选择权，因此不断解释。这既是信息延迟，也是人物塑造：她很在意自己在听者眼中是否公平、是否值得信任。

scenes.title: A childhood someone else wants to remember
scenes.titleZh: 别人也想拥有的童年
scenes.text: A seriously ill donor asks Kathy to describe Hailsham repeatedly. She realises he wants more than entertaining stories: he wants the memories to feel like his own. This gives Hailsham emotional value before readers understand it institutionally. It also complicates nostalgia, because Kathy’s conviction that she was fortunate partly grows out of comparing her childhood with another person’s more painful experience.
scenes.zh: 病重的 donor 反复要求听 Hailsham 的大小事情，并非单纯忘记了，而是想把那些画面变成自己的回忆。记忆像一种心理庇护。Kathy 对学校的感激也具有比较性：因为别人经历更差，她觉得自己幸运；这种感激不能自动证明学校没有问题。

scenes.title: The group turns cruelty into entertainment
scenes.titleZh: 群体怎样把伤害变成笑话
scenes.text: The girls watch a planned humiliation from the pavilion windows. Tommy expects selection because he plays football well; the boys instead leave him alone and move to another field. When his anger continues, the spectators become uncomfortable and explain why he deserves it. Notice how these explanations protect the observers from admitting that watching and laughing have helped make the cruelty possible.
scenes.zh: 女孩们处在旁观者的位置，似乎没有亲自设计恶作剧；但观看、模仿与笑声让伤害成为群体娱乐。Tommy 发怒太久后，她们开始不舒服，于是强调他不努力、脾气差。这是自我辩护：把问题变成受害者的缺点，便不必面对自己的参与。

scenes.title: The shirt creates a small connection
scenes.titleZh: 一件衣服建立的联系
scenes.text: Kathy approaches Tommy through a concrete concern rather than a speech about bullying: his favourite shirt may be ruined. He is surprised that she has understood its importance. His accidental blow interrupts the attempt at kindness, and Kathy eventually withdraws under the others’ gaze. The scene creates a tentative connection while showing that sympathy does not remove embarrassment, irritation or social pressure.
scenes.zh: Kathy 没有发表大道理，而是记得他珍惜什么。衣服让抽象的同情变成具体的关心。不过，她也会恼火，也怕别人观看；Tommy 则因受伤的自尊说出不友善的话。两人的联系并不完美，正因为如此，才具有真实的人际复杂性。

details.label: Kathy’s age
details.value: Thirty-one in the narrating present.
details.zh: 讲述时31岁，不是校园回忆中的年龄。

details.label: Length of caring
details.value: More than eleven years; eight months remain, bringing the total close to twelve.
details.zh: 已做十一年多，还剩八个月；不要把开头说成已经做满十二年。

details.label: The two playing fields
details.value: The boys choose teams on the North Playing Field, then run towards the South Playing Field.
details.zh: 先在 North Playing Field 选队，再向 South Playing Field 跑去。

details.label: Tommy’s shirt
details.value: A light-blue polo shirt bought at a Sale the previous month.
details.zh: 浅蓝色 polo shirt，来自上个月的 Sale。

details.label: Laura
details.value: The friend who mimics Tommy’s changing facial expressions.
details.zh: Laura 模仿 Tommy 表情，使旁观者发笑。

details.label: Miss Jody
details.value: Kathy suggests asking her for help if the mud will not wash out.
details.zh: Kathy 提到洗不掉泥点时可以找 Miss Jody。

pitfall.en: Tommy does not deliberately punch Kathy. She understands the contact as accidental. Kathy is also a participant in the watching group before she intervenes.
pitfall.zh: 不要写 Tommy 故意殴打 Kathy；她认为那是挥臂时的意外。也不要把 Kathy 写成从未参与群体冷漠的完美英雄。

chapters.questionZh: 为什么 Kathy 反复注意 Tommy 的衣服，而不只描述他的发怒？
chapters.answerZh: 衣服显示他有普通而具体的珍爱之物。Kathy 因为记得这一点而看见群体忽略的个人；但她仍怕同伴目光，所以同情并不等于完全摆脱群体压力。

chapters.title: Creativity as a social test
chapters.summary: Tommy apologises to Kathy on the crowded staircase while students pass to and from their regular medical examinations. His awkward sincerity makes her pay closer attention to his treatment. She learns that the bullying is sustained and often cruel, yet when she raises it in the dormitory, Ruth argues that Tommy must change his attitude towards creative work. Kathy explains the Exchanges: students submit artwork, receive tokens assessed by the guardians, and buy work made by others in their own year. Creativity therefore affects possessions, reputation and friendship. A later conversation with Ruth reveals how uncertain their supposedly sophisticated artistic judgments were. The narrative traces Tommy’s difficulties back to a deliberately childish elephant painting in Miss Geraldine’s class. Her exaggerated praise, intended to protect him, increases classmates’ resentment. His defensive refusal to try and their ridicule reinforce one another. Eventually the teasing weakens, although his artwork has not improved. His new calm and self-confidence change the group’s response. Kathy asks what happened and discovers that Miss Lucy privately told him he need not blame himself for lacking artistic ability. The chapter ends with the promise of a fuller conversation.
events: Tommy apologises for the accident.
The Exchanges link art, possessions and status.
Miss Lucy’s reassurance helps Tommy control his reactions.

analysis.detail: Kathy interrupts the bullying account to explain Exchanges.
analysis.effect: The apparent detour shows that Tommy’s treatment is connected to the school’s values. His suffering becomes a consequence of a social system, not just a personal disagreement with a few boys.
analysis.zh: 叙事的 digression 有解释作用：Exchanges 说明为什么艺术能力能影响人际待遇。Tommy 的困境由学校价值观与同伴行为共同形成，而非几个孩子之间的孤立冲突。

analysis.detail: Miss Geraldine’s attempt to protect Tommy makes other children resent him.
analysis.effect: Kind intentions do not guarantee helpful effects. The irony encourages a more careful account of care: adults may respond compassionately while misunderstanding the group dynamics that shape a child’s vulnerability.
analysis.zh: irony 在于善意造成更坏后果。作者让读者区分 intention 与 effect：关爱真实存在，但成人可能不了解孩子群体中的嫉妒与权力。

analysis.detail: Tommy becomes more accepted although his artwork remains weak.
analysis.effect: This separates artistic talent from personal worth. The group’s changing response reveals how reputations are sustained through repeated behaviour and expectations, rather than being objective measures of a person.
analysis.zh: 艺术没有进步，社会待遇却改善，说明受欢迎程度并非能力的客观反映。名声也由期待、反应和群体习惯维持；认可能够改变人的自我理解。

chapters.question: Why is the Exchange system relevant to Tommy’s bullying?
chapters.answer: Because creative work becomes a source of possessions and status, weak artwork is treated as a failure of character. The group mistakes conformity to its artistic values for personal worth.
chapters.zh: Tommy 在去接受体检的楼梯上向 Kathy 道歉。他表达真诚，却不懂十三岁同伴眼中的社交分寸，令 Kathy 有点尴尬，也使她开始更仔细地留意他的遭遇。欺凌并非偶发事件，而是长期排斥、嘲笑与恶作剧。Kathy 在宿舍说这样不公平，Ruth 却认为他应该先改变不认真创作的态度。接着，Kathy 解释 Exchanges：学生作品换取 tokens，再用 tokens 买同年级同学的作品。艺术因此不只是兴趣，还决定个人收藏、名声与归属。Tommy 的问题可追溯到一幅幼稚的大象水彩画：Miss Geraldine 为保护他而过度表扬，反而激起其他学生的不满。越被嘲笑，他越用故意敷衍保护自己。后来，他的作品并未进步，但脾气和自信改变，群体逐渐失去欺负他的兴趣。原来 Miss Lucy 私下告诉他，不擅长创作不等于他有错。关键是自我价值的改变，而非突然获得艺术天赋。
chapters.titleZh: 创造力怎样决定一个人的地位

orientation.en: At about thirteen, Kathy becomes more interested in Tommy’s exclusion. Her account moves back to the childhood incident that began it and forward to a later conversation with Ruth.
orientation.zh: 主要关注十三岁左右的 Tommy，但叙述会追溯更小的时候，也会插入成年 Kathy 与 Ruth 的回忆比较；不要把这些事件当成同一天发生。

chapters.summaryZh: Tommy 在去接受体检的楼梯上向 Kathy 道歉。他表达真诚，却不懂十三岁同伴眼中的社交分寸，令 Kathy 有点尴尬，也使她开始更仔细地留意他的遭遇。欺凌并非偶发事件，而是长期排斥、嘲笑与恶作剧。Kathy 在宿舍说这样不公平，Ruth 却认为他应该先改变不认真创作的态度。接着，Kathy 解释 Exchanges：学生作品换取 tokens，再用 tokens 买同年级同学的作品。艺术因此不只是兴趣，还决定个人收藏、名声与归属。Tommy 的问题可追溯到一幅幼稚的大象水彩画：Miss Geraldine 为保护他而过度表扬，反而激起其他学生的不满。越被嘲笑，他越用故意敷衍保护自己。后来，他的作品并未进步，但脾气和自信改变，群体逐渐失去欺负他的兴趣。原来 Miss Lucy 私下告诉他，不擅长创作不等于他有错。关键是自我价值的改变，而非突然获得艺术天赋。

scenes.title: An apology on the staircase
scenes.titleZh: 楼梯上的道歉
scenes.text: Students moving between medical checks create a crowded public setting for Tommy’s apology. Kathy accepts that he did not mean to hit her, but feels uncomfortable with his openly enthusiastic manner. Her response is not rejection of his kindness: it shows how adolescent codes regulate even friendly behaviour. Afterwards, she investigates incidents she hears about rather than treating his isolation as a passing joke.
scenes.zh: 楼梯是公开场合，Tommy 大声而热情地道歉，Kathy 觉得这不像十三岁男孩女孩之间应有的样子。这里体现 adolescent social codes，而不是说明她不原谅他。之后她主动追问恶作剧的细节，开始看见他承受的是长期排斥。

scenes.title: The Exchanges create a social economy
scenes.titleZh: Exchanges 也是一种地位制度
scenes.text: Four seasonal Exchanges turn student creations into possessions purchased with tokens. Guardians decide each work’s token value, and students can buy only from their own year. This encourages mutual appreciation, but also makes artistic production a public measure of worth. Kathy’s later questions about poetry expose a gap between enjoying literature and accepting that a respected poet must deserve social authority.
scenes.zh: 一年四次 Exchanges，教师决定作品值多少 tokens，学生只买同年级作品。它确实能培养欣赏，也把创作变成公开排名。Kathy 后来回想诗歌地位，发现大家未必真正理解作品，却把诗写得好的人视为更值得尊重；艺术评价与群体权力混在一起。

scenes.title: The elephant and the cycle of humiliation
scenes.titleZh: 大象画与恶性循环
scenes.text: Tommy describes making an intentionally childish elephant painting. Kathy suspects that his joking covered anxiety about not keeping up. Miss Geraldine praises it to protect him, but the class resents this apparent indulgence. Later attempts are watched so critically that he retreats into pretending not to care. The chapter explains behaviour through a cycle of shame, rather than accepting the simple label of laziness.
scenes.zh: Tommy 说大象画是开玩笑，成年 Kathy 认为这也可能掩饰落后的不安。Miss Geraldine 的好意被同学理解为偏袒；他努力时受嘲笑，便退回不在乎的姿态。分析要看到羞耻、防卫与群体反应的循环，不能只用 lazy 概括他。

scenes.title: A change without better artwork
scenes.titleZh: 没有变成艺术家，却开始改变
scenes.text: Kathy notices that Tommy no longer gives tormentors the outbursts they expect. Arthur H. tries to restart the mockery during football, but the others do not join in. Because Tommy’s creative work is still weak, Kathy recognises that something deeper has changed. Miss Lucy’s reassurance has given him a different basis for valuing himself, reducing his dependence on the group’s judgments.
scenes.zh: Arthur H. 再次模仿 Tommy 时，其他男孩不再配合。改变并非艺术水平提升，而是他不再完全接受集体对他的评价。Miss Lucy 的认可提供另一种 self-worth：缺乏某项能力，不等于整个人没有价值。

details.label: Medical examinations
details.value: Usually almost weekly in Room 18, with Nurse Trisha.
details.zh: 通常几乎每周体检，地点 Room 18，护士 Nurse Trisha。

details.label: Nurse’s nickname
details.value: Crow Face is the students’ nickname for Nurse Trisha.
details.zh: Crow Face 指 Nurse Trisha，不是另一名 guardian。

details.label: Exchange frequency
details.value: Four times yearly: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
details.zh: 一年四次，每个季节一次。

details.label: Buying rule
details.value: Students may buy work made by students in their own year.
details.zh: 只能购买同年级学生的作品。

details.label: The painting
details.value: An elephant standing in tall grass, made in Miss Geraldine’s class.
details.zh: 画的是站在高草中的大象；上课教师是 Miss Geraldine。

details.label: Poetry and craft names
details.value: Christy is admired for poetry; Jackie makes giraffes.
details.zh: Christy 以诗歌出名，Jackie 制作长颈鹿。

details.label: Arthur H.
details.value: One of Tommy’s persistent tormentors.
details.zh: Arthur H. 是经常欺负 Tommy 的学生之一。

pitfall.en: The Exchanges are not the Sales. Exchanges circulate students’ own work; Sales bring objects from outside. Miss Lucy’s reassurance does not suddenly improve Tommy’s art.
pitfall.zh: 不要把 Exchanges 与 Sales 混淆：前者交易学生作品，后者带来外界物品。Miss Lucy 改变的是 Tommy 的自我评价，不是突然提高他的绘画技能。

chapters.questionZh: 为什么分析 Tommy 被欺凌时必须提到 Exchanges？
chapters.answerZh: 因为创作能力通过 tokens、收藏和名声影响地位。群体把不符合艺术标准误解成性格有问题，令能力差异变成人际排斥的理由。

chapters.title: Madame’s recoil
chapters.summary: Tommy explains his conversation with Miss Lucy in greater detail. She had insisted that genuine difficulty with creativity was not his fault, while showing an anger that seemed directed elsewhere. She also suggested that students were not being taught enough about their futures. Kathy tries to connect these remarks to Madame’s visits and the removal of their best artwork. The Gallery is familiar as an idea, but its existence and purpose are uncertain; students have inherited the story and avoid mentioning it directly to guardians. Kathy then recalls Ruth’s theory that Madame is afraid of them rather than merely unfriendly. At about eight, six children arrange to surround her politely as she arrives. They expect the result to settle their own disagreement. Instead, Madame’s stiff recoil makes them feel that she fears physical contact with them. The children are shaken by seeing themselves through an outsider’s disturbed gaze. Kathy remembers this as a moment when vague knowledge of being different acquired an emotional reality. The chapter deepens the questions about art and education without providing their answers.
events: Tommy reports Miss Lucy’s concern about their education.
The purpose of Madame’s art collection remains uncertain.
The children test Madame’s reaction to their presence.

analysis.method: Simile and a shift in perspective
analysis.detail: Kathy compares Madame’s fear to fear of spiders.
analysis.effect: The comparison makes the children experience themselves as objects of involuntary disgust. Its force comes from changing who is looking and who is being looked at, rather than from any physical attack.
analysis.zh: spider simile 将孩子放进令人本能畏惧的位置。震撼来自 gaze 的变化：原本他们在观察 Madame，现在被迫想象她眼里的自己。

analysis.detail: A playful experiment ends in collective silence and distress.
analysis.effect: The abrupt emotional change marks the movement from curiosity to painful understanding. Learning how someone sees you can matter more than learning a new factual statement about yourself.
analysis.zh: 由玩笑、挑战转向沉默，表现从 curiosity 到 emotional understanding。并非增加一条新知识就等于理解；这次遭遇让“不同”成为切身感受。

analysis.detail: Students invoke the Gallery among themselves but avoid questioning guardians.
analysis.effect: Control operates through embarrassment and collective expectations as well as explicit instructions. The students help preserve the boundary between what can be repeated and what can be investigated.
analysis.zh: 沉默不只来自成人命令，也来自学生的尴尬与默契。他们可以反复说 Gallery，却不能追究它是什么；knowledge 与 questioning 被分隔开。

chapters.question: Why does the successful test of Ruth’s theory make the children unhappy?
chapters.answer: They expected to settle a disagreement, but Madame’s response makes them see themselves as frightening outsiders. The experiment turns an abstract suspicion into a painful experience of being different.
chapters.zh: 池塘边，Tommy 更详细地讲述 Miss Lucy 的话：如果他确实努力过仍不擅长创作，就不应该责怪自己。她说话时压抑着怒气，却不是对他生气；她还认为学生对自身未来了解得不够。Kathy 开始把这件事与 Madame 收走优秀作品联系起来。Gallery 虽然人人谈论，却来自学生间代代相传的说法，教师并未正式解释，学生自己也遵守不向教师提问的默契。随后，Kathy 回忆八岁左右的测试：Ruth 怀疑 Madame 不是高傲，而是害怕他们。六个孩子等她到校，故意礼貌地迎面围上去。结果她僵住，仿佛害怕被他们碰到。原本带游戏性质的挑战，变成一次痛苦的自我认识：他们第一次强烈感受到，外界可能把自己看成令人恐惧的异类。重点是情感理解的突然到来，而不是本章已经揭晓了所有秘密。
chapters.titleZh: 从 Madame 的目光中看见自己

orientation.en: The pond conversation continues at around thirteen, then Kathy remembers the children testing Madame when they were about eight. The Gallery’s real purpose is still unknown here.
orientation.zh: 先继续十三岁左右的池塘谈话，再回到八岁左右测试 Madame 的事件。此时学生还不知道 Gallery 的真正用途，分析必须保留这种未知。

chapters.summaryZh: 池塘边，Tommy 更详细地讲述 Miss Lucy 的话：如果他确实努力过仍不擅长创作，就不应该责怪自己。她说话时压抑着怒气，却不是对他生气；她还认为学生对自身未来了解得不够。Kathy 开始把这件事与 Madame 收走优秀作品联系起来。Gallery 虽然人人谈论，却来自学生间代代相传的说法，教师并未正式解释，学生自己也遵守不向教师提问的默契。随后，Kathy 回忆八岁左右的测试：Ruth 怀疑 Madame 不是高傲，而是害怕他们。六个孩子等她到校，故意礼貌地迎面围上去。结果她僵住，仿佛害怕被他们碰到。原本带游戏性质的挑战，变成一次痛苦的自我认识：他们第一次强烈感受到，外界可能把自己看成令人恐惧的异类。重点是情感理解的突然到来，而不是本章已经揭晓了所有秘密。

scenes.title: A guardian’s anger without an explanation
scenes.titleZh: 有怒气，却没有完整解释
scenes.text: Tommy distinguishes Miss Lucy’s anger from anger at him. This matters because he is used to adults telling him to try harder. Her reassurance changes that familiar pattern, but her remarks about what students are taught introduce a larger uncertainty. Kathy listens actively, asking what links artistic creativity and donations. Neither child can yet turn these clues into a complete explanation.
scenes.zh: Tommy 特别强调 Lucy 不是对他生气，因为他早已习惯被要求再努力。她第一次改变了责备他的逻辑，却又提到教育不足。Kathy 追问 art 和 donations 为什么同时出现；这种主动联系很重要，但读者不能把线索误写成两人已经知道答案。

scenes.title: Everyone knows about something nobody has seen
scenes.titleZh: 人人知道、却无人确证的 Gallery
scenes.text: Kathy remembers Amanda C. praising her childhood work as suitable for the Gallery. Years later, Carole H. accidentally mentions it to Mr. Roger and immediately recognises the social mistake. The contrast shows how the Gallery can organise ambition without being openly discussed. Its power rests partly on inherited stories and partly on students’ own caution around adults.
scenes.zh: Amanda C. 早年用 Gallery 夸奖 Kathy；Carole H. 在 Mr. Roger 面前提起它却立刻意识到失言。Gallery 因而既是荣誉标准，又是禁忌话题。权威不必天天明令禁止，学生之间传承的习惯也会维持沉默。

scenes.title: Ruth turns a theory into a test
scenes.titleZh: Ruth 把猜想变成测试
scenes.text: The children prepare by watching the selection of artwork in the billiards room and then tracking Madame’s arrival. Their plan involves no attack: they will walk towards her together and politely separate. This careful construction matters because the emotional damage comes from a minimal response. Madame need only freeze and recoil for the children to recognise a feeling they had not expected to confront.
scenes.zh: 他们通过 billiards room 里的作品准备判断 Madame 何时来访，再轮流望风。计划不是袭击她，而是突然一起迎面走去、礼貌经过。她没有大喊大叫；正是那种克制却明显的畏缩，使孩子感到自己被当成异类。

scenes.title: The experiment changes the observers
scenes.titleZh: 测试者也被测试改变
scenes.text: Once Madame has passed, the children no longer feel triumphant. Hannah looks close to tears, and even Ruth is shaken. The question shifts from whether Ruth was right to what it feels like to be seen this way. Kathy’s adult narration describes the encounter as a new, troubling reflection of the self: familiar identity becomes strange when filtered through someone else’s fear.
scenes.zh: 结果证明 Ruth 猜对了，却没有带来胜利感。Hannah 几乎哭出来，Ruth 也受到震动。问题从“她是否怕我们”变成“被别人这样看待是什么感觉”。这是 othering 的心理后果：别人眼里的自己，突然与一直熟悉的自己不一样。

details.label: The pond
details.value: Kathy and Tommy connect Miss Lucy’s comments with questions about the Gallery.
details.zh: 池塘谈话连接 Lucy 的话、未来与 Gallery。

details.label: Amanda C.
details.value: A child one year older who praises young Kathy’s modelling-clay work.
details.zh: 比 Kathy 大一岁，曾夸她的黏土作品。

details.label: Carole H.
details.value: Accidentally refers to the Gallery in front of Mr. Roger.
details.zh: 在 Mr. Roger 面前无意提到 Gallery 的学生。

details.label: Madame’s visits
details.value: Usually twice yearly, sometimes three or four times.
details.zh: 通常一年两次，有时三四次。

details.label: Madame’s clothes
details.value: A sharp grey suit; on the test day she carries a briefcase.
details.zh: 灰色套装；测试当天带着公文包。

details.label: The test group
details.value: Six children, about eight years old, led by Ruth.
details.zh: 六名孩子，约八岁，Ruth 带头。

details.label: The lesson before the test
details.value: Mr. Frank teaches spelling in Room 9.
details.zh: 测试前是 Mr. Frank 在 Room 9 上的拼写课。

pitfall.en: The scene proves that Madame recoils from contact, not that she consciously wants to hurt the children. Her nationality is disputed by the students here; the Gallery’s purpose remains unresolved.
pitfall.zh: 本章能确定的是 Madame 对接触感到畏惧，不能直接断言她想伤害孩子。她是法国人还是比利时人，学生有争论；Gallery 用途此时仍是谜。

chapters.questionZh: 为什么成功证明 Ruth 的猜想，反而让孩子们难过？
chapters.answerZh: 他们原本只想证明谁对谁错，却从 Madame 的反应中看见自己被视为令人畏惧的异类。抽象的“我们不同”变成切身的被排斥感。

chapters.title: Small possessions, small freedoms
chapters.summary: Kathy explains why childhood memories are necessary for understanding her later relationships. After the unsettling encounter with Madame, students avoid probing her activities, but a dispute about tokens briefly raises questions of ownership. Some argue that work taken for the Gallery should earn compensation. Roy J. approaches Miss Emily, and the school eventually awards a small number of tokens. During discussion, Polly T. asks why Madame takes the work at all; Miss Lucy says the reason is important but does not explain it. Kathy then distinguishes the monthly Sales, which bring outside goods, from the Exchanges of student artwork. Miss Emily appears both protective and intimidating: students respect her authority even when they cannot understand her speeches. Finally, Kathy recalls Ruth inviting her to ride imaginary horses. Ruth first offers Bramble, forbids use of a crop, gives instructions for other horses such as Daffodil, and eventually allows Kathy to ride her favourite, Thunder. The enjoyable game establishes Ruth’s power to grant access and set rules. It ends with an invitation for Kathy to join Miss Geraldine’s secret guards, connecting friendship with shared fantasy and loyalty.
events: Students seek tokens for art selected by Madame.
The Sales bring second-hand possessions into Hailsham.
Kathy joins Ruth’s imaginative games.

analysis.detail: Miss Emily controls school rules; Ruth controls entry to imaginary games.
analysis.effect: Placing these relationships in the same chapter invites comparison without making them identical. Both forms of authority combine security, belonging and unequal access to decisions, helping explain how dependence can feel comforting as well as restrictive.
analysis.zh: 学校权威与儿童游戏并置，可比较但不能简单画等号：它们都通过安全感、归属和资格建立关系。控制并不总以暴力出现，也可能存在于令人珍惜的亲密关系中。

analysis.detail: Tokens make students calculate the value of art and outside possessions.
analysis.effect: Objects provide ways to personalise a highly communal life. The controversy shows a developing sense of ownership, while also revealing how little power students have over the larger purpose for which their work is collected.
analysis.zh: 共同生活中，物品帮助学生建立私人身份。tokens controversy 说明他们已懂得所有权与公平，却只能影响补偿多少，仍不了解作品被使用的总体目的。

analysis.detail: Ruth’s horses have distinct names, rules and levels of permitted access.
analysis.effect: The detailed make-believe is not empty decoration. It offers freedom of imagination while rehearsing hierarchy: Kathy gains favour by accepting Ruth’s knowledge and following her instructions. Genuine pleasure and power coexist.
analysis.zh: 马的名字、性格和规则让 make-believe 变成社会秩序。想象带来乐趣，也让 Kathy 通过遵守 Ruth 的规定获得认可；分析应同时看到快乐与权力。

chapters.question: How does the horse game establish the pattern of Kathy and Ruth’s friendship?
chapters.answer: It gives both girls genuine pleasure and makes Kathy feel specially chosen, but Ruth controls the horses, rules and invitation. Affection and dependence develop together.
chapters.zh: Kathy 解释：要理解后来的人际关系，就必须先整理 Hailsham 的童年。学生因 Madame 的反应而不愿继续深究，但 tokens controversy 暂时让所有权问题浮现：最优秀、最值钱的作品被拿走，是否应该得到补偿？Roy J. 向 Miss Emily 提出要求，最后学校同意给少量 tokens。Polly T. 进一步问 Madame 为什么拿作品，Miss Lucy 只说原因重要，将来希望有人解释。接着必须区分 Sales 与 Exchanges：Sales 每月带来外界物品，Exchanges 交易学生自己的作品。Miss Emily 一方面令人害怕，一方面使学生觉得安全，她的权威并不依赖频繁惩罚。最后叙述回到七八岁：Ruth 邀 Kathy 骑想象中的马，先给她 Bramble，要求不能用马鞭；Daffodil 要向后仰；最喜欢的 Thunder 起初不许骑，后来才允许。游戏充满快乐，也由 Ruth 控制规则与资格。之后她邀请 Kathy 加入保护 Miss Geraldine 的 secret guard，友谊、归属与服从由此交织。
chapters.titleZh: 所有权、权威与想象中的马

orientation.en: Kathy revisits the tokens controversy at about ten, describes the Sales and Miss Emily, then goes further back to the start of her friendship with Ruth at seven or eight.
orientation.zh: 本章不是顺时序：先讲约十岁的 tokens controversy，再讲学校日常与 Miss Emily，最后回到七八岁时 Kathy 与 Ruth 成为朋友的经过。

chapters.summaryZh: Kathy 解释：要理解后来的人际关系，就必须先整理 Hailsham 的童年。学生因 Madame 的反应而不愿继续深究，但 tokens controversy 暂时让所有权问题浮现：最优秀、最值钱的作品被拿走，是否应该得到补偿？Roy J. 向 Miss Emily 提出要求，最后学校同意给少量 tokens。Polly T. 进一步问 Madame 为什么拿作品，Miss Lucy 只说原因重要，将来希望有人解释。接着必须区分 Sales 与 Exchanges：Sales 每月带来外界物品，Exchanges 交易学生自己的作品。Miss Emily 一方面令人害怕，一方面使学生觉得安全，她的权威并不依赖频繁惩罚。最后叙述回到七八岁：Ruth 邀 Kathy 骑想象中的马，先给她 Bramble，要求不能用马鞭；Daffodil 要向后仰；最喜欢的 Thunder 起初不许骑，后来才允许。游戏充满快乐，也由 Ruth 控制规则与资格。之后她邀请 Kathy 加入保护 Miss Geraldine 的 secret guard，友谊、归属与服从由此交织。

scenes.title: Who owns the best work?
scenes.titleZh: 最优秀的作品属于谁？
scenes.text: The children have learned to value objects through tokens, so having their best work removed becomes both an honour and a material loss. Roy J. takes the demand for compensation to Miss Emily. The eventual small payment compromises between the two positions. The students can debate the price of what is taken while still lacking an explanation of why it is taken at all.
scenes.zh: 作品既是荣誉，也是可换取物品的资源，学生因此产生矛盾。Roy J. 争取补偿，学校以少量 tokens 妥协。但他们能讨论“值多少钱”，却不知道“为什么拿走”；可商量的局部问题，掩盖了仍无法追问的根本问题。

scenes.title: A question everyone wants and fears
scenes.titleZh: 人人好奇、却害怕有人问的问题
scenes.text: Polly T. directly asks Miss Lucy why Madame takes their creations. Others resent the breach of an unwritten rule even while eagerly awaiting the answer. Lucy offers reassurance about an important purpose instead of explaining it. The group soon returns to safer discussion of tokens. Their relief reveals that the desire for knowledge competes with a desire to avoid unsettling the familiar school order.
scenes.zh: Polly T. 问出大家想知道的问题，其他人却先责怪她破坏默契，再期待答案。Lucy 没有解答，话题回到 tokens 后大家反而松口气。这里不是孩子完全不想知道，而是好奇与维护安全感同时存在，后者常压过前者。

scenes.title: The outside arrives in boxes
scenes.titleZh: 装在箱子里的外界
scenes.text: Monthly Sales allow students to obtain clothes, toys and other items not made at Hailsham. A white van promises novelty, though the actual goods often disappoint. The noise and occasional fighting contrast with the Exchanges’ more restrained atmosphere. Miss Emily’s later lectures frame behaviour in terms of privilege and responsibility, but the children often respond to her authority more clearly than to her actual meaning.
scenes.zh: 白色货车每月带来外界衣服、玩具等物品；希望往往大于实际收获。Sales 的喧闹与 Exchanges 的安静形成对比。发生争抢后，Miss Emily 强调 privilege；学生感到自己让她失望，却不一定听懂论述，说明情感服从可以先于理解。

scenes.title: The imaginary stable
scenes.titleZh: 想象中的马厩与友谊规则
scenes.text: Ruth singles Kathy out from other children and offers access to her imaginary horses. Kathy’s decision not to invent horses of her own lets Ruth retain expertise and control. The two genuinely enjoy themselves, but Ruth can also stop the game and accuse Kathy of handling the horses badly. The later secret-guard invitation extends the same pattern: inclusion feels special because Ruth controls its conditions.
scenes.zh: Ruth 特意选择 Kathy，使她感到被看重。Kathy 说自己没有马，让 Ruth 保持拥有者与指导者的位置。两人确实玩得投入，但 Ruth 也能突然终止、指责她。加入 secret guard 延续同一结构：被接纳令人幸福，资格却由 Ruth 掌握。

details.label: Roy J.
details.value: The student a year above Kathy who takes the tokens issue to Miss Emily.
details.zh: Roy J. 比 Kathy 大一年级，代表提出 tokens 要求。

details.label: Polly T.
details.value: Asks Miss Lucy why Madame takes their artwork.
details.zh: Polly T. 直接问 Madame 为什么拿作品。

details.label: Sales
details.value: Monthly, in the Dining Hall; outside goods arrive in a large white van.
details.zh: 每月一次，在 Dining Hall；外界物品由白色大货车送来。

details.label: Bramble
details.value: The first horse Ruth offers Kathy; she must not use her crop on him.
details.zh: 第一匹给 Kathy 骑的马；不能对他用 crop（马鞭）。

details.label: Thunder
details.value: Ruth’s best and favourite horse; initially described as too dangerous, later offered to Kathy.
details.zh: Ruth 最喜欢的马；先说太危险，后来才让 Kathy 骑。

details.label: Daffodil
details.value: Ruth tells Kathy to lean much farther back when riding her.
details.zh: 骑 Daffodil 时要明显向后仰；原文以 she 指这匹马。

details.label: The secret guard invitation
details.value: Ruth asks whether Miss Geraldine is Kathy’s special favourite before inviting her.
details.zh: Ruth 先确认 Kathy 是否特别喜欢 Miss Geraldine，再邀请加入。

pitfall.en: Bramble, Thunder and Daffodil are imaginary horses. Thunder is initially withheld but Kathy eventually rides him. Do not state that she is never allowed to ride Thunder.
pitfall.zh: Bramble、Thunder、Daffodil 都是想象中的马。Thunder 起初不让骑，但 Kathy 后来确实骑到；不要把前半段限制误当成最终结果。

chapters.questionZh: 骑马游戏怎样建立 Kathy 与 Ruth 友谊的基本模式？
chapters.answerZh: Kathy 因被选中而快乐，两人也真心投入游戏；同时，马匹、规则、结束时间和加入资格都由 Ruth 决定，所以亲密与不平等并存。

chapters.title: The rules of make-believe
chapters.summary: Kathy describes the secret guard, a shifting group led by Ruth that claims to protect Miss Geraldine from kidnapping. Frightening stories about the woods make the imagined danger plausible, although the guardians dismiss those stories. The group collects suspicious-looking incidents rather than confronting anyone, keeping its fantasy safe from testing. Ruth’s claim to possess earlier knowledge gives her authority to include or expel members. When Kathy discovers that Ruth cannot really teach chess, she walks away from their game and is subsequently excluded from the guard. Yet Kathy angrily defends the group when another former member, Moira B., calls it childish. She even invents evidence, revealing that the fantasy’s survival is not Ruth’s responsibility alone. The chapter then moves to Ruth’s new pencil case. Ruth hints that Miss Geraldine gave it to her, making Kathy resent the apparent claim to special affection. Kathy pretends to have examined the Sales register, hoping to expose the story. Ruth’s distress, however, changes the emotional meaning of the victory. Kathy recognises a shared desire to be loved specially by a guardian and regrets hurting her friend.
events: The secret guard invents threats around Miss Geraldine.
Ruth excludes Kathy after the chess disagreement.
Kathy challenges the story behind Ruth’s pencil case.

analysis.detail: Kathy supplies invented evidence even after being excluded.
analysis.effect: The episode prevents readers from blaming only a manipulative leader. The group survives because members gain comfort and identity from believing, so they help maintain the very structure that can injure them.
analysis.zh: Kathy 主动补造证据，说明不能只责怪 Ruth 操纵。成员从幻想得到身份和安慰，也帮助维持会伤害自己的结构；complicity 可以源于需要归属。

analysis.detail: Kathy offers more than one explanation for rejecting Moira.
analysis.effect: The narrator does not reduce childhood motives to a single neat cause. Her uncertainty makes room for contradictory impulses and demonstrates the difficulty of understanding one’s former self.
analysis.zh: 成年 Kathy 没有给出唯一动机，保留忠诚、害怕、羞耻等可能。这种 qualification 显示自我解释的困难，而不是分析上的弱点。

analysis.method: A turning point in emotional perspective
analysis.detail: Kathy’s triumph collapses when she sees Ruth’s distress.
analysis.effect: The pencil case shifts from a symbol of unfair superiority to evidence of a wish for special care. The change encourages readers to understand Ruth’s need without denying that her hints hurt other people.
analysis.zh: pencil case 先象征偏爱与炫耀，后显露被爱的渴望。读者可以理解 Ruth 的脆弱，同时承认她的暗示确实伤人；同情不等于替行为免责。

chapters.question: Why does Kathy defend the secret guard after Ruth has excluded her?
chapters.answer: The group still represents belonging and a protected shared world. Kathy’s loyalty and reluctance to abandon that world outweigh the chance to join Moira in exposing it; the narrator deliberately leaves more than one motive possible.
chapters.zh: secret guard 是 Ruth 领导、人数会变化的小团体，自称保护 Miss Geraldine 免遭绑架。树林传说虽然被 guardians 否认，却让孩子觉得危险真实存在。他们不断搜集所谓证据，却总避免当面对质，因此幻想不会轻易被事实推翻。Ruth 利用“以前就知道的秘密”决定谁能加入、谁被赶走。Kathy 买了棋具，希望 Ruth 教她 chess，却发现她把所有棋子都说成走 L 形。Kathy 生气离开，后来也被排除。但另一个被排除的 Moira B. 说 secret guard 幼稚时，Kathy 反而激烈辩护，甚至编造自己偷听到绑架计划的证据：维持幻想的并不只有 Ruth。接着，几年后的 pencil case 事件显示 Ruth 渴望 Miss Geraldine 的特殊关爱。Kathy 假称查过 Sales register，试图拆穿文具盒来源；看到 Ruth 几乎哭出来后，她意识到自己攻击的是朋友脆弱的被爱愿望。真相、嫉妒、忠诚与同情因而发生冲突。
chapters.titleZh: 明知脆弱，仍要守住的幻想

orientation.en: The secret guard belongs to the girls’ childhood around seven or eight. The pencil-case episode occurs roughly three years later. Kathy links them through Ruth’s attachment to Miss Geraldine.
orientation.zh: secret guard 发生在约七八岁；pencil case 事件约晚三年。Kathy 以两件事都涉及 Miss Geraldine 为联系，而不是按同一时段连续讲述。

chapters.summaryZh: secret guard 是 Ruth 领导、人数会变化的小团体，自称保护 Miss Geraldine 免遭绑架。树林传说虽然被 guardians 否认，却让孩子觉得危险真实存在。他们不断搜集所谓证据，却总避免当面对质，因此幻想不会轻易被事实推翻。Ruth 利用“以前就知道的秘密”决定谁能加入、谁被赶走。Kathy 买了棋具，希望 Ruth 教她 chess，却发现她把所有棋子都说成走 L 形。Kathy 生气离开，后来也被排除。但另一个被排除的 Moira B. 说 secret guard 幼稚时，Kathy 反而激烈辩护，甚至编造自己偷听到绑架计划的证据：维持幻想的并不只有 Ruth。接着，几年后的 pencil case 事件显示 Ruth 渴望 Miss Geraldine 的特殊关爱。Kathy 假称查过 Sales register，试图拆穿文具盒来源；看到 Ruth 几乎哭出来后，她意识到自己攻击的是朋友脆弱的被爱愿望。真相、嫉妒、忠诚与同情因而发生冲突。

scenes.title: A guard that gathers evidence but never acts
scenes.titleZh: 一直搜证，却从不行动的 guard
scenes.text: Members interpret ordinary conversations among adults as signs of a kidnapping plot. Ruth can appeal to information from before Kathy joined whenever her leadership is challenged. Yet they postpone confronting supposed conspirators and keep Miss Geraldine uninformed. These choices protect the group’s belief from contradiction. The guard provides a feeling of purpose and importance even though its evidence remains unreliable.
scenes.zh: 成人普通的交谈被解释为阴谋；Ruth 还可诉诸 Kathy 加入前的秘密。大家却不断推迟对质，也不告诉 Miss Geraldine。这样的规则保护幻想不被验证，让团体持续拥有使命感。不要把这些孩子的“证据”当作小说确认的真实绑架计划。

scenes.title: The woods as an inherited fear
scenes.titleZh: 被代代传下来的树林恐惧
scenes.text: Stories of death, punishment and exclusion surround the woods beyond Hailsham. Guardians deny them, but older students insist that younger children will learn the terrible truth later. The fear becomes a tool within the children’s own society when they force Marge K. to look towards the trees. The scene shows how vulnerable children can reproduce cruelty using beliefs they have inherited.
scenes.zh: 树林故事由学生流传，教师反而否认。年长学生声称将来才会知道真相，使恐惧难被消除。孩子们还强迫 Marge K. 看树林惩罚她。被恐惧控制的人也会利用恐惧控制别人；不能直接声称所有传说都是教师编造的。

scenes.title: Why Kathy will not side with Moira
scenes.titleZh: 为什么 Kathy 不愿与 Moira 联手
scenes.text: After the chess dispute, Kathy is excluded from a conversation in Room 20. Moira B., expelled earlier, seems a natural ally. Kathy instead invents a claim that she personally overheard the kidnappers. Her adult account considers different explanations: loyalty to Ruth, or unwillingness to step beyond a comforting framework. The uncertainty preserves the emotional complexity of defending a group that has hurt her.
scenes.zh: Kathy 被排除后，Moira 理应是同伴，但她却编造亲耳听到阴谋的证据反驳 Moira。成年叙述提出不止一种解释：对 Ruth 的忠诚，或害怕放弃熟悉的安全框架。这种不确定使人物更复杂；她既知道幻想脆弱，又需要它带来的归属。

scenes.title: Winning the argument, losing the satisfaction
scenes.titleZh: 赢了揭穿，却没有胜利感
scenes.text: Ruth’s pencil-case story is conveyed through hints rather than a direct claim, which makes it difficult to challenge. Kathy devises a bluff involving the Sales register instead of actually checking it. When Ruth appears close to tears, Kathy’s anger turns into remorse. The episode asks whether exposing an untruth is always a simple moral victory when that untruth expresses a vulnerable wish for affection.
scenes.zh: Ruth 用暗示而非直接陈述，难以被正面质问；Kathy 也并未真正查到记录，而是在诈她。看到 Ruth 受伤后，她不再享受揭穿。这里不是说欺骗永远合理，而是让读者思考：事实正确与行为体贴未必总能同时满足。

details.label: Membership
details.value: Roughly six to ten members; Ruth controls admission and expulsion.
details.zh: 约六到十人，人数随 Ruth 决定变化。

details.label: Person protected
details.value: Miss Geraldine, not Miss Lucy or Miss Emily.
details.zh: 保护的是 Miss Geraldine。

details.label: Suspected adults
details.value: Miss Eileen is suspected; Mr. Roger is later added after a conversation is watched.
details.zh: 孩子怀疑 Miss Eileen，后来因观察到交谈也怀疑 Mr. Roger；只是猜测。

details.label: Chess mistake
details.value: Ruth says every piece moves in an L-shape.
details.zh: Ruth 把骑士的 L 形走法错误推广到所有棋子。

details.label: Moira B.
details.value: A former secret-guard member who challenges the fantasy.
details.zh: Moira B. 是先前已被排除的成员。

details.label: Pencil case
details.value: Deep tan with circled red dots and a furry pom-pom on the zip.
details.zh: 深黄褐色，有红色圆点，拉链带毛绒小球。

details.label: Sales register bluff
details.value: Kathy pretends to have browsed the register while talking to monitor Christopher C.
details.zh: Kathy 假称与 monitor Christopher C. 聊天时翻过记录；没有真正证明来源。

pitfall.en: Kathy never verifies the register before confronting Ruth; she bluffs. The kidnapping plot and woodland stories are children’s beliefs, not established facts.
pitfall.zh: Kathy 用的是 bluff，并非已经查证文具盒来源。绑架和树林传说都要标明为儿童想象或传闻，不能写成事实。

chapters.questionZh: 为什么被 Ruth 排除后，Kathy 仍保护 secret guard 的幻想？
chapters.answerZh: 那个团体仍代表归属与熟悉的安全世界。忠诚、害怕失去幻想以及不愿接受被排除的身份，都可能使她维护它；叙述刻意保留多重动机。

chapters.title: A song, a tape, a lost corner
chapters.summary: Kathy tries to repair the damage from exposing Ruth’s pencil-case story, but their shared habit of indirectness makes a straightforward apology difficult. When Midge A. innocently asks about the pencil case, Kathy protects Ruth by suggesting that its origin must remain secret. Ruth begins looking for a way to return the kindness. Kathy then explains the students’ belief that lost possessions end up in Norfolk, a comforting misunderstanding of Miss Emily’s geography lesson. Her own precious possession is a Judy Bridgewater cassette, Songs After Dark. She hides the cover because it shows a cigarette, while Hailsham’s strong warnings about smoking make even the image feel dangerous. The song that matters to her is track three, Never Let Me Go. Kathy privately imagines a woman holding a longed-for baby, although she knows this is not the literal story of the lyrics. Madame sees her dancing with a pillow and cries, leaving Kathy confused. Later the cassette disappears for unknown reasons. Ruth searches and gives her a different recording, Twenty Classic Dance Tunes. Its musical mismatch matters less than the care behind it: the gift becomes a treasured sign of friendship.
events: Kathy supports Ruth after their dispute.
Madame sees Kathy’s private dance and cries.
The tape disappears; Ruth offers another recording.

analysis.detail: The two tapes matter for different emotional reasons.
analysis.effect: One recording holds Kathy’s private fantasy; the other preserves Ruth’s effort to help. Their value exceeds usefulness or price, showing how ordinary objects become containers for otherwise hard-to-express attachment.
analysis.zh: 两盘磁带分别承载私人渴望与朋友关爱。物品价值不等于用途或价格；symbolism 来自人物赋予它们的关系意义，而不是物品天然具有某种固定含义。

analysis.detail: The Norfolk theory and Kathy’s reading of the song are factually inaccurate.
analysis.effect: Their inaccuracy does not make them emotionally empty. Each gives shape to a wish: that loss may be reversible, or that something precious can be held safely. The novel asks what imaginative stories help people endure.
analysis.zh: Norfolk 想象与歌曲解读都未必正确，却表达真实需要：希望失去可以挽回、珍贵之物可以留住。分析可以区分 factual truth 与 emotional truth。

analysis.detail: Kathy observes Madame’s crying but cannot explain it.
analysis.effect: The reader receives the scene through the child’s uncertainty and the adult narrator’s controlled disclosure. Tears suggest an inner response, but their meaning remains open at this point, resisting a premature claim about Madame’s motives.
analysis.zh: limited perspective 使读者看见泪水，却暂时不能确定原因。不要用后文答案替代本章孩子的未知；延迟解释本身就是叙事效果。

chapters.question: Why does Kathy treasure a replacement tape whose music she does not particularly like?
chapters.answer: Its value comes from Ruth’s recognition of her distress and attempt to help. Kathy reads the gift as evidence of care, so its emotional significance outweighs its musical suitability.
chapters.zh: 文具盒事件后，Kathy 想修复关系，却因为双方一直靠暗示交流，难以直接道歉。Midge A. 天真地问起 pencil case 时，Kathy 说来源必须保密，替 Ruth 维护了颜面；Ruth 因而寻找回报关爱的机会。接下来，Norfolk 被误认为全国遗失物会去的地方：孩子把地理课中的 lost corner 与校内失物招领处联系起来，这种误读提供“失去的东西仍可能找回”的安慰。Kathy 珍爱的磁带是 Judy Bridgewater 的 Songs After Dark。封面有香烟，她因学校严格禁烟而把封面翻转藏起。真正吸引她的是第三首 Never Let Me Go：她把它想象成终于得到孩子的母亲紧抱婴儿，尽管知道这不完全符合歌词。Madame 看见她抱着枕头跳舞后落泪，却没有解释。磁带后来不知为何消失；Ruth 找不到，便送她 Twenty Classic Dance Tunes。音乐并不相似，但礼物的价值来自朋友的用心。
chapters.titleZh: 丢失的磁带与保留下来的关爱

orientation.en: The chapter follows the pencil-case quarrel, explains the Norfolk belief, and returns to Kathy’s treasured cassette at eleven. Later recollections are signposted by the narrator.
orientation.zh: 本章把友谊修复、Norfolk 想象和十一岁时的磁带记忆连在一起。叙述偶尔提及成年后的回想，核心仍是这些童年事件怎样获得情感意义。

chapters.summaryZh: 文具盒事件后，Kathy 想修复关系，却因为双方一直靠暗示交流，难以直接道歉。Midge A. 天真地问起 pencil case 时，Kathy 说来源必须保密，替 Ruth 维护了颜面；Ruth 因而寻找回报关爱的机会。接下来，Norfolk 被误认为全国遗失物会去的地方：孩子把地理课中的 lost corner 与校内失物招领处联系起来，这种误读提供“失去的东西仍可能找回”的安慰。Kathy 珍爱的磁带是 Judy Bridgewater 的 Songs After Dark。封面有香烟，她因学校严格禁烟而把封面翻转藏起。真正吸引她的是第三首 Never Let Me Go：她把它想象成终于得到孩子的母亲紧抱婴儿，尽管知道这不完全符合歌词。Madame 看见她抱着枕头跳舞后落泪，却没有解释。磁带后来不知为何消失；Ruth 找不到，便送她 Twenty Classic Dance Tunes。音乐并不相似，但礼物的价值来自朋友的用心。

scenes.title: An apology expressed through protection
scenes.titleZh: 通过保护面子来道歉
scenes.text: Kathy cannot easily say that she regrets the register bluff because the original claim was never openly stated. She instead supports Ruth’s suggestion of special favour. When Midge asks about the pencil case, Kathy intervenes before Ruth must explain. The repair is emotionally effective but depends on sustaining the misleading story, showing how honesty and care can pull in different directions within friendship.
scenes.zh: 原来的谎言是暗示式的，所以道歉也难以直接说清。Kathy 选择在 Midge 追问时帮 Ruth 保住面子。关系确实得到修复，但代价是继续维持误导；friendship 中 honesty 与 care 并不总能轻易协调。

scenes.title: Norfolk turns geography into hope
scenes.titleZh: Norfolk：地理被改造成希望
scenes.text: Miss Emily lacks a calendar photograph of Norfolk and describes the county’s isolated position on England’s east coast. Students connect this with Hailsham’s own lost-property corner and imagine a national destination for missing things. Kathy and Ruth remember believing it literally at first, while Tommy later thinks it was always a joke. The disagreement itself shows how adult memory reshapes childhood belief.
scenes.zh: Miss Emily 没有 Norfolk 的日历照片，又谈到它偏在东边。孩子联想到校内 Lost Corner，便想象遗失物都运到那里。Kathy 与 Ruth 记得最初真信过，Tommy 却觉得一直是玩笑；同一往事在不同人的记忆中意义会改变。

scenes.title: The song becomes a private story
scenes.titleZh: 歌曲变成 Kathy 的私人故事
scenes.text: Kathy listens for a repeated phrase and builds her own scene of a mother holding a desperately wanted baby. She recognises that her interpretation does not fit all the lyrics, yet keeps it because it expresses something important to her. Madame’s tears introduce another interpretation that Kathy cannot access. The episode presents art as a meeting point for feelings that remain difficult to explain openly.
scenes.zh: Kathy 不是认真逐句理解歌词，而是抓住一句话创造自己的母亲故事。她知道解释不完全符合歌词，却仍需要它。Madame 的泪水提示别人可能看到另一层意义，但本章尚未说明。art 因而承载私密情感，也暴露人与人之间理解的距离。

scenes.title: A different tape, a meaningful gift
scenes.titleZh: 不同的磁带，同样重要的礼物
scenes.text: When the cassette vanishes, Kathy hides the extent of her distress. Ruth notices anyway, searches discreetly, and eventually gives her a substitute from a Sale. Kathy is initially disappointed because it is ballroom orchestra music, but understands that Ruth lacks the musical knowledge to recognise the difference. Gratitude grows from recognising intention, turning an unsuitable recording into a valuable emotional object.
scenes.zh: Kathy 不想公开自己有多难过，Ruth 却注意到了，并低调帮忙。替代磁带是舞厅管弦乐，Kathy 一开始失望，随后意识到 Ruth 不懂音乐类型差异。价值因此不在音乐是否合适，而在朋友认真尝试弥补失去。

details.label: Midge A.
details.value: Asks innocently about Ruth’s pencil case during Mr. Roger’s art lesson.
details.zh: Midge A. 是在 Mr. Roger 的美术课上问起文具盒的人。

details.label: Norfolk
details.value: A county on England’s east coast, associated by the children with lost property.
details.zh: 英格兰东岸郡；“失物都去那里”是孩子的误解。

details.label: Album and singer
details.value: Songs After Dark by Judy Bridgewater; recording dated 1956.
details.zh: 专辑 Songs After Dark，歌手 Judy Bridgewater，录音年份1956。

details.label: Favourite track
details.value: Track three: Never Let Me Go.
details.zh: 最珍爱的歌曲是第三首 Never Let Me Go。

details.label: The cover
details.value: Judy wears a purple satin dress and holds a burning cigarette.
details.zh: 紫色缎面裙、手持点燃的香烟；Kathy 因香烟藏起封面。

details.label: Madame’s visit
details.value: Kathy holds a pillow as an imagined baby while dancing in the dormitory.
details.zh: Kathy 在宿舍抱枕头当婴儿；Madame 在门外看到并哭泣。

details.label: Ruth’s replacement
details.value: Twenty Classic Dance Tunes, orchestral ballroom music.
details.zh: Ruth 送的是 Twenty Classic Dance Tunes，不是原专辑的另一份。

pitfall.en: Ruth does not recover the original tape or give Kathy another copy of it. The original disappears for an unknown reason; Kathy explicitly says there is no basis for linking that loss to Madame.
pitfall.zh: Ruth 没找回原带，也没送同专辑副本。原带为什么消失仍不明；Kathy 明说没有理由把失踪与 Madame 联系起来。

chapters.questionZh: 为什么 Kathy 会珍惜一盘自己并不喜欢其音乐的替代磁带？
chapters.answerZh: 它证明 Ruth 注意到她的痛苦并努力帮忙。礼物承载关系中的关爱，所以情感价值超过音乐是否合适。

chapters.title: Knowing without understanding
chapters.summary: Kathy describes the final Hailsham years as more serious than the warm blur of earlier childhood. After her conversation with Tommy, she watches Miss Lucy for clues and notices remarks that the rest of the class overlook. The central incident occurs when students shelter from rain at the pavilion. Hearing Peter J. and Gordon discuss becoming actors in America, Miss Lucy interrupts. She explicitly tells the students that their futures are already organised around donating vital organs, and insists that hearing facts without understanding them is inadequate. Kathy then explores how this state of partial knowledge developed. Lessons about sex and health also contained information about donation, while students’ attention often remained elsewhere. Tommy later proposes a deliberate strategy of telling children things before they could understand; Kathy treats this as a theory, not a proven explanation. An earlier prank about Tommy’s elbow supposedly unzipping illustrates how frightening bodily ideas became jokes. Kathy’s failure to correct the lie also exposes the uneasy relationship between protecting feelings and telling truth. After Lucy’s speech, donation jokes fade and the subject becomes sombre, although sustained open discussion remains difficult.
events: Miss Lucy directly challenges the students’ career fantasies.
Kathy distinguishes earlier partial knowledge from genuine understanding.
After the speech, donation jokes fade and the subject becomes sombre.

analysis.detail: The students can possess information while failing to grasp its implications.
analysis.effect: The central contradiction distinguishes knowledge from understanding. It suggests that a system can disclose facts and still limit genuine awareness through timing, context and emotional habits; this is more complex than a simple claim that every adult always lies.
analysis.zh: told and not told 的 paradox 区分知道与理解。时间、情境、注意力与情绪都能让事实被听见却不被消化，因此不能只把 Hailsham 概括为从未说过真话。

analysis.detail: Imagined unzipping becomes a recurring donation joke.
analysis.effect: Joking acknowledges the body’s vulnerability while preventing sustained attention to it. When the jokes fade, the same subject becomes harder to dismiss, showing that silence can mean different things at different stages of understanding.
analysis.zh: humour 让学生接触可怕事实，却不必停留思考。笑话消失后，沉默不再只是尴尬，也可能是认识重量后的沉重；同一种 silence 可以有不同含义。

analysis.method: Parallel between personal and institutional care
analysis.detail: Kathy withholds the truth about the prank to avoid upsetting Tommy.
analysis.effect: This smaller dilemma echoes the larger problem of protection through partial knowledge. Kathy’s concern is sincere, yet the omission leaves Tommy exposed to humiliation. The parallel invites scrutiny of care’s effects without claiming the situations are identical.
analysis.zh: Kathy 为保护感情而不说真相，缩小呈现 protection 与 truth 的矛盾。她的好意真实，但隐瞒仍有伤害；这种 parallel 帮助分析制度，不是把她与所有成人简单等同。

chapters.question: How can students know about donations and still be “told and not told”?
chapters.answer: Facts may be familiar without being emotionally or practically understood. Distraction, jokes and awkward silences keep their implications at a distance; Lucy tries to connect the information to the students’ own possible lives.
chapters.zh: Kathy 把最后几年与早年的金色回忆区分开：十三岁后，她开始主动观察 Miss Lucy 的异常言行。十五岁左右，学生躲雨时，Peter J. 与 Gordon 谈论去美国当演员；Lucy 突然打断，明确说明他们的未来已被安排，要捐出重要器官。核心是 told and not told：听过事实，不等于真正理解它对自己人生的意义。Kathy 随后回顾知识怎样进入他们脑中：性教育、健康与 donation 常被放在一起，学生更关注性与同伴关系，未来命运便退到背景。Tommy 后来认为教师故意在他们太小时提供信息，但 Kathy 没有把这个解释当作已证实的阴谋。较早的手肘恶作剧也显示，身体恐惧如何被转化成笑话；Kathy 不愿使 Tommy 难过，反而没告诉他真相。Lucy 讲话后，donation 笑话减少，话题变得严肃沉重。不是一切毫无变化，而是理解加深后仍难坦然面对。
chapters.titleZh: 听说了，却没有真正理解

orientation.en: Kathy surveys ages thirteen to sixteen. The central pavilion speech occurs when they are fifteen; the elbow prank is an earlier memory from around thirteen, not a later consequence of the speech.
orientation.zh: 本章总览十三至十六岁。Miss Lucy 的 pavilion speech 发生在十五岁左右；“手肘会拉开”的恶作剧是十三岁左右的较早记忆，不是演说之后发生。

chapters.summaryZh: Kathy 把最后几年与早年的金色回忆区分开：十三岁后，她开始主动观察 Miss Lucy 的异常言行。十五岁左右，学生躲雨时，Peter J. 与 Gordon 谈论去美国当演员；Lucy 突然打断，明确说明他们的未来已被安排，要捐出重要器官。核心是 told and not told：听过事实，不等于真正理解它对自己人生的意义。Kathy 随后回顾知识怎样进入他们脑中：性教育、健康与 donation 常被放在一起，学生更关注性与同伴关系，未来命运便退到背景。Tommy 后来认为教师故意在他们太小时提供信息，但 Kathy 没有把这个解释当作已证实的阴谋。较早的手肘恶作剧也显示，身体恐惧如何被转化成笑话；Kathy 不愿使 Tommy 难过，反而没告诉他真相。Lucy 讲话后，donation 笑话减少，话题变得严肃沉重。不是一切毫无变化，而是理解加深后仍难坦然面对。

scenes.title: Learning to notice what others miss
scenes.titleZh: 开始注意别人忽略的细节
scenes.text: Kathy now watches Miss Lucy rather than simply joining the class mood. During a discussion of wartime prison camps, classmates turn electric fences into a joke, while Lucy briefly looks disturbed. The reader sees the contrast between children’s playful response and an adult’s troubling associations. Kathy’s later narration also admits that she may now organise these scattered incidents more coherently than she understood them then.
scenes.zh: 讨论战争中的 prison camps 时，学生拿电网开玩笑，Lucy 却短暂流露不安。Kathy 开始观察成人情绪，但成年叙述也承认：今天看起来连贯的线索，当年未必已被她理解。要分清 noticing 与 understanding。

scenes.title: Peter’s imagined future meets Lucy’s intervention
scenes.titleZh: 想象中的演员人生遇上直接说明
scenes.text: Peter J. explains that he and Gordon were imagining becoming actors; Lucy points out that they had discussed America. She broadens her response to everyone and rejects ordinary career expectations, including supermarket work. Her intervention is meant to make their prospects comprehensible, not merely to add a new rule. The students’ discomfort shows how difficult it is to connect known information with an imagined personal future.
scenes.zh: Peter J. 与 Gordon 只是想象当演员，Lucy 却指出连普通职业路线也不属于他们既定的人生。她要处理的是理解，不是宣布新的纪律。学生会说早就知道，却仍能想象完全不同的未来，正暴露 knowledge 尚未转化成自我认识。

scenes.title: The elbow prank turns anxiety into entertainment
scenes.titleZh: 手肘恶作剧怎样利用身体焦虑
scenes.text: Christopher H. tells Tommy that a cut on the elbow can open dramatically if he bends it. Others reinforce the claim until Tommy asks Kathy to help keep his arm straight at night. She knows the warning is false, but agrees because she cannot bear to disappoint him. He discovers the deception before she acts. The incident turns a concern for health into both social humiliation and a language for joking about donation.
scenes.zh: Christopher H. 利用 Tommy 对身体健康的担忧编造手肘会拉开的说法。别人不断附和，Tommy 便请 Kathy 帮忙固定手臂。她知道是假话，却因怕伤害他的感情而没说实话；结果关心与欺骗纠缠，身体焦虑又成为群体取笑的材料。

scenes.title: What changes after the speech?
scenes.titleZh: 演说之后究竟改变了什么？
scenes.text: Kathy says classmates initially discuss Lucy’s behaviour more than her message. Yet she later identifies a real change: the running donation jokes fade, and avoidance becomes serious rather than merely embarrassed. This distinction matters. The speech does not produce an easy, complete understanding or shared plan, but neither does it leave everyone untouched. Emotional recognition develops unevenly and may make speech harder instead of easier.
scenes.zh: 起初，学生更谈论 Lucy 是否失态，而非她讲的内容；但 Kathy 也明确说后来笑话减少，回避变得沉重严肃。应避免“一点作用也没有”的简化。理解加深可能使人更难开口，因为现在回避的已经是知道其重量的事情。

details.label: Age during the speech
details.value: About fifteen, in their last year at Hailsham.
details.zh: 演说时约十五岁，处于离校前最后一年。

details.label: Triggering conversation
details.value: Peter J. and Gordon discuss becoming actors, with America as a possible destination.
details.zh: Peter J. 与 Gordon 想象去美国当演员。

details.label: Location and weather
details.value: The pavilion veranda during a downpour.
details.zh: 大雨中，在 pavilion 的 veranda（廊台）躲雨。

details.label: The elbow prank
details.value: Christopher H., from the year above, starts the false warning.
details.zh: 比他们高一年级的 Christopher H. 发起谣言。

details.label: Proposed splint
details.value: Tommy brings a thick ruler and asks Kathy to help strap his arm.
details.zh: Tommy 拿来厚尺子，想让 Kathy 帮忙固定手臂。

details.label: Gary B.
details.value: His third helping of pudding becomes the target of the imaginary organ joke.
details.zh: Gary B. 食量很大，第三份布丁成为恶作剧式想象的对象。

details.label: Tommy’s later theory
details.value: Information may have been timed before children could understand; Kathy does not fully endorse this.
details.zh: Tommy 提出“故意太早告知”的解释，Kathy 并未完全认可。

pitfall.en: Do not say the speech reveals every fact for the first time, or that it changes nothing. Kathy records both earlier partial knowledge and a later, more serious attitude. Tommy’s explanation of deliberate timing remains a theory.
pitfall.zh: 不要说 Lucy 第一次透露全部事实，也不要说演说毫无影响。学生此前已有零散知识，此后态度更沉重；Tommy 的“精心安排时间”说仍是解释，不是证实事实。

chapters.questionZh: 为什么学生知道 donation，却仍可以说是 told and not told？
chapters.answerZh: 他们熟悉事实，却未把后果与自己的人生真正连接。分心、笑话、尴尬和沉默维持距离；Lucy 要促成的是理解，而不只是再增加一个知识点。

chapters.title: Uneasy adolescence
chapters.summary: Kathy begins by describing a private game in which she imagines Hailsham as a quiet home shared with only a few people. While looking for such an empty view, she hears a strange hissing sound and discovers Miss Lucy in Room 22, furiously covering handwritten pages with pencil marks. Kathy feels ashamed and disturbed but cannot explain what she has witnessed. She also notices Tommy becoming unusually sensitive. A joke about mud on his shirt nearly provokes an outburst, and he abruptly withdraws when she shows him Patricia C.’s admired calendar. Kathy assumes his difficulties mainly concern his breakup with Ruth, overlooking a possible connection with art and Miss Lucy. The chapter then examines adolescents’ confusion about relationships. Guardians speak positively about intimacy while rules make privacy difficult, and students exaggerate their experience without questioning one another closely. Kathy feels pressure to catch up and considers Harry C. because she thinks he would be considerate and discreet. She prepares anxiously, treating experience almost like a skill to master before a more important relationship. Ruth and Tommy’s separation interrupts this plan, leaving Kathy’s feelings less settled than her practical approach suggested.
events: Kathy witnesses Miss Lucy’s unexplained distress.
Tommy’s troubled behaviour returns.
Kathy reflects on sexual expectations and Harry C.

analysis.detail: An imagined peaceful Hailsham gives way to Lucy’s dark, agitated room.
analysis.effect: The contrast makes emotional disturbance emerge from within familiar safety. The school is not simply presented as either comforting or threatening; Kathy’s attachment coexists with experiences she cannot explain.
analysis.zh: 安静想象与黑暗房间形成 contrast，使不安从熟悉的安全内部出现。学校不是纯粹天堂或纯粹恐怖场所；依恋与困惑同时存在。

analysis.detail: Kathy misreads Tommy’s behaviour mainly through the breakup.
analysis.effect: Readers see the older narrator recognise a connection her younger self missed. This creates distance between experiencing and narrating, reminding us that an event’s meaning often becomes clear only after other information arrives.
analysis.zh: 成年 Kathy 看出年轻时错过的联系，形成 experiencing self 与 narrating self 的距离。并非每个反应当场就能解释，后来的信息会重组意义。

analysis.detail: Relationship experience replaces creativity as a measure of belonging.
analysis.effect: The repeated structure shows that changing ages do not remove the desire for approval. Kathy’s anxieties belong to ordinary adolescence, while the school’s inconsistent guidance makes that familiar uncertainty sharper.
analysis.zh: 评价标准从艺术转成青春期经验，群体认可的需求却不变。这个 recurring pattern 既呈现普通青春期，也显示 Hailsham 矛盾指导带来的特殊困惑。

chapters.question: Why does Kathy fail to connect Tommy’s reaction to the calendar with Miss Lucy?
chapters.answer: She assumes his old artistic difficulties are behind him and interprets his mood through the more immediate breakup. Her later account exposes this missed connection and the limits of her younger understanding.
chapters.zh: 这一章先写 Kathy 的私人游戏：她寻找没有人的视角，短暂想象 Hailsham 是只有少数人居住的安静家园。随后，她循着嘶嘶声来到 Room 22，看见 Miss Lucy 用铅笔愤怒地涂黑原本整齐的蓝色字迹，却不知道文字内容和原因。她感到羞耻、困惑，选择不立即告诉别人。Tommy 也变得敏感：别人开泥点玩笑时他差点发作；Kathy 展示 Patricia C. 的精美日历，他也突然离开。Kathy 把这些反应主要归因于他与 Ruth 分手，没想到还可能涉及创作和 Lucy。后半章转向青春期：教师说亲密关系自然美好，学校规则却几乎不给私人空间；学生又夸大经验，彼此不追问。Kathy 因而觉得自己落后，考虑与安静、可靠的 Harry C. 建立身体关系，并把它当作将来重要关系前的准备。重点是同伴比较、成人信息矛盾与情感不确定，而不是把她简化成轻浮。
chapters.titleZh: 成人世界尚未解释清楚，青春期已经到来

orientation.en: Many students have turned sixteen. Kathy observes Miss Lucy privately, notices Tommy’s instability, and looks back on the pressures surrounding relationships and sexual maturity.
orientation.zh: 许多学生此时已满十六岁。Kathy 同时面对 Lucy 的异常、Tommy 的情绪变化与青春期的同伴压力；这些线索互相遮蔽，而非各自独立。

chapters.summaryZh: 这一章先写 Kathy 的私人游戏：她寻找没有人的视角，短暂想象 Hailsham 是只有少数人居住的安静家园。随后，她循着嘶嘶声来到 Room 22，看见 Miss Lucy 用铅笔愤怒地涂黑原本整齐的蓝色字迹，却不知道文字内容和原因。她感到羞耻、困惑，选择不立即告诉别人。Tommy 也变得敏感：别人开泥点玩笑时他差点发作；Kathy 展示 Patricia C. 的精美日历，他也突然离开。Kathy 把这些反应主要归因于他与 Ruth 分手，没想到还可能涉及创作和 Lucy。后半章转向青春期：教师说亲密关系自然美好，学校规则却几乎不给私人空间；学生又夸大经验，彼此不追问。Kathy 因而觉得自己落后，考虑与安静、可靠的 Harry C. 建立身体关系，并把它当作将来重要关系前的准备。重点是同伴比较、成人信息矛盾与情感不确定，而不是把她简化成轻浮。

scenes.title: A quiet house inside a crowded school
scenes.titleZh: 在拥挤学校中想象一个安静的家
scenes.text: Kathy’s private game requires her to find an empty view and temporarily block out surrounding noise. She imagines sharing the house with only five or six others. The fantasy is small and ordinary, yet revealing: she seeks a form of domestic privacy within institutional life. It also prepares the interruption, when her attempt to create calm leads her to an adult’s concealed distress.
scenes.zh: 她寻找无人画面、屏蔽声音，想象只与五六个人共同生活。这个幻想不像宏大逃跑计划，更像对普通家庭式私密空间的向往。紧接着她撞见 Lucy 的痛苦，使“安静之家”的愿望与学校隐藏的不安形成对照。

scenes.title: The pages in Room 22
scenes.titleZh: Room 22 里被涂黑的字迹
scenes.text: The sound Kathy follows is Miss Lucy’s pencil repeatedly scraping over written sheets. Kathy can identify anger and concealment, but not the content of the writing or its exact significance. Neither person begins an open conversation. Kathy leaves wishing she had not seen it. The scene shows a breakdown in communication across the child–guardian boundary, even when evidence of distress is physically visible.
scenes.zh: 声音来自铅笔用力划过纸张。Kathy 看得出愤怒，却不知道内容；两人也没有谈清。可见的痛苦不自动产生理解：child 与 guardian 之间有一道不知如何跨越的沟通边界。不要编造被涂黑的文件内容。

scenes.title: A calendar becomes a missed clue
scenes.titleZh: 日历成为被错过的线索
scenes.text: Patricia C.’s small calendar contains carefully observed Hailsham scenes and is much admired. Kathy proudly shows it to Tommy, expecting shared pleasure, but he closes off and leaves. Her adult account recognises that this should have pointed towards his old insecurity about creativity. At the time, however, the breakup seemed the more obvious explanation, demonstrating how an available story can obscure another cause.
scenes.zh: Patricia C. 的小日历画着校园场景，Kathy 因买到而自豪；Tommy 却不愿看。成年她明白这应指向 creativity 的旧伤，当时却只想到分手。limited perspective 也包括解释习惯：一个看似合理的原因，会遮住另一个原因。

scenes.title: Growing up becomes another comparison
scenes.titleZh: 成长也变成必须赶上的标准
scenes.text: Students maintain a tacit agreement not to challenge claims about relationship experience. Kathy feels left behind even while suspecting exaggeration. The pressure resembles the earlier requirement to be creative: personal development becomes something measured against peers. Her choice of Harry is practical and cautious, showing a desire for control and preparedness, but the changing relationship between Ruth and Tommy unsettles that apparently orderly plan.
scenes.zh: 大家默契地不追问经验真假，Kathy 即使怀疑夸张，仍觉得自己落后。这与早年必须 creative 的压力相似：个人成长被群体变成标准。她选择 Harry 时考虑可靠、体贴与保密，显示控制不确定性的愿望，而关系变化又打乱计划。

details.label: Room 22
details.value: The small, dim room where Kathy discovers Miss Lucy.
details.zh: 小而昏暗的 Room 22；不能与常规体检的 Room 18 混淆。

details.label: Writing materials
details.value: Neat blue handwriting is covered with heavy black pencil marks.
details.zh: 整齐蓝色字迹被黑色铅笔线条覆盖。

details.label: Patricia C.
details.value: Two years younger than Kathy; admired for drawing.
details.zh: 比 Kathy 低两个年级，以绘画受到赞赏。

details.label: Calendar subject
details.value: Small pencil sketches of Hailsham life, not photographs of English counties.
details.zh: 画的是 Hailsham 生活素描，不是 Miss Emily 用的英国各郡照片日历。

details.label: Ruth and Tommy
details.value: They had been publicly a couple for about six months before the breakup.
details.zh: 分手前公开交往约六个月。

details.label: Harry C.
details.value: The boy Kathy considers because he seems experienced, quiet, decent and discreet.
details.zh: Kathy 认为 Harry 有经验、安静可靠、不爱传播私事。

details.label: The peer-pressure parallel
details.value: Kathy compares pressure to have experience with earlier pressure to be creative.
details.zh: 她明确把青春期经验压力与早年 creativity 压力联系起来。

pitfall.en: The content of Lucy’s crossed-out pages is never identified in this scene. The chapter describes Kathy considering and postponing a plan involving Harry, not a completed encounter.
pitfall.zh: 被 Lucy 涂黑的文字内容不明，不能说已知是某种报告。Kathy 对 Harry 的想法是计划与推迟，不是本章已经发生的行动。

chapters.questionZh: 为什么 Kathy 当时没有把 Tommy 对日历的反应与 Miss Lucy 联系起来？
chapters.answerZh: 她以为艺术方面的旧问题已经过去，把当下情绪主要理解为分手造成。成年叙述回头指出这个误判，显示年轻视角的局限。

chapters.title: A departure without an explanation
chapters.summary: After Ruth and Tommy separate, Cynthia E. remarks that Kathy seems the natural person to take Ruth’s place. Hannah’s hints reinforce the possibility, confusing Kathy’s earlier plans involving Harry C. Ruth then asks Kathy to persuade Tommy to reunite with her, stressing Kathy’s special ability to reach him. Kathy agrees, although her concern for Tommy and her own uncertain feelings make the role complicated. When she finds him practising football, she assumes that his troubled behaviour comes from the breakup. Tommy explains that the deeper cause is Miss Lucy. During a recent private conversation, Lucy reversed her earlier reassurance and insisted that art mattered, both as evidence and for Tommy’s own benefit. She also admitted that he did not understand important things about Hailsham and the wider world, without explaining them. Kathy listens, then returns to Ruth’s request, while Tommy argues that their approaching departure makes careful choices more important. The next day Charlotte F. spreads the news that Miss Lucy has left permanently. Miss Emily had announced this unexpectedly during another class’s Music Appreciation lesson. That evening Tommy and Ruth reunite, but their reconciliation does not resolve the disturbing questions raised by Lucy’s departure.
events: Ruth asks Kathy to speak to Tommy.
Miss Lucy revises her advice about creativity.
Miss Lucy leaves; Ruth and Tommy reunite.

analysis.detail: Ruth praises Kathy’s special understanding of Tommy while asking her to restore the couple.
analysis.effect: The language of trust makes refusal difficult. Rather than treating Ruth as a simple villain, examine how genuine dependence and self-interest can operate together, and how Kathy’s loyalty complicates her own uncertain desires.
analysis.zh: trust 与 compliment 使拒绝变难。Ruth 可以真实依赖 Kathy，同时也为自己争取关系；分析应看两者并存，不把人物扁平化成纯粹恶人。

analysis.detail: Miss Lucy changes her advice but leaves the meaning of evidence unexplained.
analysis.effect: The reversal destabilises Tommy’s recovered self-worth and enlarges the mystery of creativity. Information produces further uncertainty because it arrives without enough context to guide his choices.
analysis.zh: reversal 动摇 Tommy 好不容易建立的自信。新信息没有带来清楚方向，反而扩大谜团；这延续全书对“告知了多少”与“能理解多少”的区分。

analysis.detail: Part One closes with an unexplained adult departure and an apparently repaired relationship.
analysis.effect: The outward return to order does not resolve the underlying conflict. Readers leave Hailsham with the students while questions about education, art and identity remain open, giving the transition an unsettled rather than reassuring quality.
analysis.zh: 表面秩序恢复：两人复合、生活继续；深层问题却未解决。第一部这种 ending 使离校不是圆满毕业，而是带着未解疑问进入下一阶段。

chapters.question: Why is the ending of Part One unresolved even though Ruth and Tommy reunite?
chapters.answer: Their outward reconciliation leaves Lucy’s reversal and departure unexplained. The students must prepare to leave Hailsham without understanding the purpose of their art or all the forces shaping their relationships.
chapters.zh: Ruth 与 Tommy 分手后，Cynthia E. 认为 Kathy 很自然会成为下一任女友；Hannah 的暗示也强化这一可能，使 Kathy 对 Harry 的计划变得混乱。Ruth 随后请求她说服 Tommy 复合，强调只有 Kathy 最懂他、最值得信任。Kathy 同意，却同时担心 Tommy 再受伤。她找到练球的 Tommy，以为他的烦恼都是分手造成；Tommy 却说真正困扰他的是 Miss Lucy。Lucy 在一次私人谈话中推翻以前“不必担心创作”的安慰，强调艺术既是 evidence，也对他本人有价值，但仍不解释证据究竟证明什么。Kathy 听完又回到复合任务，Tommy 则表示正因为快离校，更不能仓促决定。次日，Charlotte F. 传来 Lucy 永久离开的消息；原来 Miss Emily 在另一班的 Music Appreciation 课上突然宣布。当天晚上 Tommy 与 Ruth 复合，Ruth 感谢 Kathy；然而关系恢复并不意味着学校的谜团或人物的内在困惑已经解决。
chapters.titleZh: 离开前，关系与秘密都未解决

orientation.en: During their final summer at Hailsham, Kathy is pulled between possible closeness to Tommy and loyalty to Ruth. News of Miss Lucy’s departure closes Part One.
orientation.zh: 最后一个夏天，Kathy 一方面可能更接近 Tommy，一方面被 Ruth 请求帮助复合。Miss Lucy 离开的消息使第一部结束，却没有解开艺术与学校的秘密。

chapters.summaryZh: Ruth 与 Tommy 分手后，Cynthia E. 认为 Kathy 很自然会成为下一任女友；Hannah 的暗示也强化这一可能，使 Kathy 对 Harry 的计划变得混乱。Ruth 随后请求她说服 Tommy 复合，强调只有 Kathy 最懂他、最值得信任。Kathy 同意，却同时担心 Tommy 再受伤。她找到练球的 Tommy，以为他的烦恼都是分手造成；Tommy 却说真正困扰他的是 Miss Lucy。Lucy 在一次私人谈话中推翻以前“不必担心创作”的安慰，强调艺术既是 evidence，也对他本人有价值，但仍不解释证据究竟证明什么。Kathy 听完又回到复合任务，Tommy 则表示正因为快离校，更不能仓促决定。次日，Charlotte F. 传来 Lucy 永久离开的消息；原来 Miss Emily 在另一班的 Music Appreciation 课上突然宣布。当天晚上 Tommy 与 Ruth 复合，Ruth 感谢 Kathy；然而关系恢复并不意味着学校的谜团或人物的内在困惑已经解决。

scenes.title: A possible future suggested by other people
scenes.titleZh: 别人先替 Kathy 想好了下一步
scenes.text: Cynthia E.’s offhand remark matters because she stands outside Kathy’s close circle and seems perceptive rather than manipulative. Hannah’s nudge then suggests that the same expectation is circulating among friends. Kathy begins to imagine a different possibility with Tommy. Her later reflections on Harry show that her apparently clear plan was never as emotionally detached as she had presented it.
scenes.zh: Cynthia E. 不属于核心小团体，因此一句随口判断反而像旁观者的客观眼光。Hannah 再次暗示后，Kathy 开始意识到自己与 Tommy 的可能性。她原本看似理性的 Harry 计划因此动摇，显示感情未必能按事先设计推进。

scenes.title: Ruth asks the person who understands Tommy
scenes.titleZh: Ruth 请求最懂 Tommy 的人帮忙
scenes.text: Ruth tells Kathy she trusts her and praises her courage through Tommy’s reported admiration. The request honours Kathy’s closeness to Tommy while using that closeness to restore Ruth’s relationship with him. Kathy asks whether Ruth is serious and will avoid hurting him again. The conversation is therefore both intimate cooperation and a source of pressure, not a simple agreement without emotional cost.
scenes.zh: Ruth 以信任与赞美请求 Kathy，承认她最能与 Tommy 沟通，却又借这种亲近来恢复自己的关系。Kathy 追问她是否认真、是否还会伤害他，说明答应不是毫无顾虑。亲密合作与情感压力在同一场对话里同时存在。

scenes.title: Lucy reverses the reassurance
scenes.titleZh: Lucy 推翻曾经给予的安慰
scenes.text: While helping Lucy carry materials towards the Orangery, Tommy is invited into her study. She says her earlier advice did him a disservice and urges him to begin creating seriously. The new word evidence makes the Gallery seem more important, but does not explain its purpose. Tommy tries to reassure her by promising physical fitness for donation; this answer fails to meet the concern she is struggling to express.
scenes.zh: Tommy 帮 Lucy 搬东西，进入 Orangery 的 study 后听到新的要求。evidence 使艺术似乎与某个重大目的有关，但用途仍未知。他强调自己身体好、能做好 donation，反而显示两人理解不在同一层面：他用制度规定的价值回答她对更广阔人生的忧虑。

scenes.title: A departure followed by reconciliation
scenes.titleZh: 离开消息之后的复合
scenes.text: Charlotte F. brings news just after Mr. Chris’s Culture Briefing. Another class had expected Miss Lucy for Music Appreciation, but Miss Emily took over and unexpectedly announced her permanent departure during discussion of Beethoven. Kathy wants to tell Tommy herself, but arrives too late. His empty expression contrasts with others’ excitement. He reunites with Ruth that evening, leaving the reader to consider the emotional pressure surrounding that choice.
scenes.zh: 消息在 Mr. Chris 的 Culture Briefing 后传来。另一班本等 Lucy 上 Music Appreciation，却由 Emily 代课，并在谈 Beethoven 时突然宣布离职。Kathy 想亲口告诉 Tommy，却发现他已知道、神情空洞。当天的复合不能轻率归功于她劝说成功；Lucy 的离开改变了情绪背景。

details.label: Cynthia E.
details.value: Suggests Kathy is the natural successor after Ruth and Tommy separate.
details.zh: Cynthia E. 首先直接提出 Kathy 可能接替 Ruth。

details.label: Walkmans
details.value: Students share one headset in groups during the final summer.
details.zh: 最后一个夏天，学生围坐轮流听同一个 Walkman 耳机。

details.label: Ruth’s request
details.value: She asks Kathy to help her get back together with Tommy.
details.zh: Ruth 请 Kathy 帮她与 Tommy 复合。

details.label: Lucy’s study
details.value: In the Orangery; Tommy helps carry flipcharts and box files.
details.zh: study 位于 Orangery；Tommy 帮搬 flipcharts 与 box files。

details.label: A new word about art
details.value: Lucy calls art evidence but does not explain what it proves.
details.zh: Lucy 说艺术是 evidence，但没有说明证明什么。

details.label: Charlotte F.
details.value: Brings news that Miss Lucy has left Hailsham.
details.zh: Charlotte F. 传来 Miss Lucy 离开的消息。

details.label: Two different lessons
details.value: Mr. Chris teaches Culture Briefing; Miss Emily announces the departure during Music Appreciation while discussing Beethoven.
details.zh: Mr. Chris 教 Culture Briefing；Miss Emily 在 Music Appreciation 谈 Beethoven 时宣布离开，别把两个课堂混为一谈。

pitfall.en: Miss Lucy’s mention of evidence does not yet reveal the Gallery’s purpose. Kathy also cannot prove her persuasion caused the reunion; Lucy’s departure intervenes before Ruth and Tommy get back together.
pitfall.zh: 本章 evidence 仍未揭示 Gallery 用途。也不能确定复合就是 Kathy 劝说的成果：中间发生了 Lucy 离开的重大事件。

chapters.questionZh: 既然 Ruth 与 Tommy 已复合，为什么第一部结尾仍有未解决感？
chapters.answerZh: 复合只恢复了表面关系，Lucy 为什么改口与离开仍未解释；学生即将离校，却仍不清楚艺术用途，也未完全理解影响自己关系的力量。

chapters.title: Rehearsing adulthood
chapters.summary: Part Two begins after Kathy, Ruth, Tommy and five other Hailsham students move to the Cottages, a former farm. They expect another version of school, but there are no guardians: Keffers maintains the property without offering the personal guidance they miss. The newcomers initially stay together, frightened by freedoms they have little experience using. Their unfinished essays provide a reassuring connection to Hailsham; Kathy’s subject is Victorian novels. Over time, reading, conversation and relationships make the place feel more familiar. Ruth works especially hard to look mature. She changes her public behaviour with Tommy to match older residents, whom the newcomers call veterans. Kathy notices that these models of adulthood have themselves borrowed gestures from television. When Ruth interrupts Kathy’s reading of Daniel Deronda by explaining its plot, Kathy challenges both her pretended knowledge and her imitation of the couples. Ruth retaliates with a remark about Kathy’s relationships with veterans. The disagreement matters because both girls feel that an unspoken loyalty has been broken. Growing up creates new performances and new insecurities rather than a clean break with childhood.
events: The friends move into the Cottages.
Veterans provide models of adult behaviour.
Kathy questions Ruth’s imitation of those models.

analysis.detail: The supposedly mature residents borrow gestures from fictional television couples.
analysis.effect: The model of authentic adulthood turns out to be another performance. This does not make the students emotionless copies: it reveals a recognisable human need to learn belonging from the available examples.
analysis.zh: irony 在于被奉为真实、成熟的榜样本身也是模仿。不能因此说学生没有真实感情；相反，寻找行为范本表现了普遍的人类归属需求。

analysis.detail: Adult Kathy places the frightened arrival beside later memories of relaxed intellectual life.
analysis.effect: Her contrasting images resist a simple story of successful independence. Comfort develops, but underneath it she recognises a continuing dependence on the group.
analysis.zh: 成年 Kathy 把最初害怕的画面与后来的轻松生活并置。变化确实发生了，但她同时看见：他们始终依赖彼此，独立并不完整。

analysis.detail: The unfinished essay acquires value after the move.
analysis.effect: A school task becomes a link to a lost community. Its changing significance shows that the importance of an object or activity depends on memory and relationships, not only on practical achievement.
analysis.zh: essay 的象征意义来自关系的变化。它从任务变成了 emotional anchor，说明回忆可以赋予普通物品和活动新的价值。

chapters.question: What is ironic about Ruth’s idea of mature behaviour?
chapters.answer: She imitates veterans whose own mannerisms come from fictional television relationships.
chapters.zh: The Cottages 是 liminal space：看似更自由，未来却仍然被安排。
chapters.titleZh: 排练一种借来的成年生活
chapters.summaryZh: 第二部分从 Hailsham 到 Cottages 的过渡开始。Kathy、Ruth、Tommy 等八名学生来到一座改建的农场，以为这里会是“高年级版 Hailsham”，却发现没有 guardians 照顾他们。负责设施的 Keffers 冷淡而不愿解释规则，旧 essay 因而成为连接过去的精神支点。表面上，他们可以外出、阅读和建立关系，但刚来时仍紧紧聚在一起，不知道如何使用自由。Ruth 最努力学习 veterans 的“成熟”：她改变与 Tommy 告别的方式，却没有发现老生的动作也是从电视里学来的。Kathy 看穿这种 imitation，在读 Daniel Deronda 时被 Ruth 指点情节，终于反击。Ruth 随即拿 Kathy 与老生交往的事情刺她。关键不只是两人吵架，而是她们都觉得对方破坏了默契：Ruth 需要朋友支持自己的新形象，Kathy 则需要私人信任不被用来攻击自己。成年生活因此延续了童年对身份、地位与归属的焦虑。

orientation.en: The first months at the Cottages, remembered by adult Kathy. Eight students arrive from Hailsham; the residents already there become their social models.
orientation.zh: 时间来到离开 Hailsham 后的最初几个月。成年 Kathy 回忆当时的陌生感；八名新生把先到的 veterans 当作学习对象。

scenes.title: Freedom without reassurance
scenes.titleZh: 有自由，却没有安全感
scenes.text: The Cottages offer more movement and less supervision than Hailsham, but the newcomers hardly leave at first. They have never learned ordinary distances, journeys or independent routines through experience. Keffers expects chores to be done yet refuses the emotional role of a guardian. Their hesitation therefore shows how a protected upbringing can continue to shape behaviour even when visible restrictions are reduced.
scenes.zh: Cottages 的监管减少了，可学生最初几乎不出门。他们在地图上学过地方，却没有真正安排过生活。Keffers 只管事务，不提供 guardian 式的安慰。这里说明：外在限制变少，并不等于内心已经具备自由行动的信心。

scenes.title: An essay as a connection
scenes.titleZh: essay 成为情感上的连接
scenes.text: At Hailsham the leaving essays had seemed unimportant. At the Cottages, the same task gains value because it comes from a familiar world. Kathy’s later daydreams about improving her Victorian-novel essay show that its meaning survives beyond academic usefulness. The essay offers continuity: it lets her imagine herself as a student with intellectual interests rather than only as someone carrying out an assigned role.
scenes.zh: 离校前似乎不重要的 essay，到新环境反而变得珍贵，因为它来自熟悉的 Hailsham。Kathy 成年后仍会想如何重写它。它的价值超出作业本身：它保存了一个爱阅读、有思想的自我，而不只是制度安排给她的身份。

scenes.title: Imitating the imitators
scenes.titleZh: 模仿那些也在模仿的人
scenes.text: Ruth adopts the veterans’ understated couple behaviour, including a light touch near Tommy’s elbow when parting. Kathy has identified other veterans’ mannerisms on television and suspects the same source here. Their quarrel while Kathy reads exposes different needs: Ruth wants her performance supported, while Kathy resents being treated as inferior. The chapter makes social learning look ordinary and moving, while showing how easily it becomes competitive.
scenes.zh: Ruth 学老生轻拍手肘的告别方式，Tommy 起初甚至不知道该如何配合。Kathy 发现部分老生动作来自电视，也怀疑这个动作如此。两人的争执揭示不同需求：Ruth 想得到支持，Kathy 不愿被轻视。模仿既是成长的尝试，也是争夺地位的方式。

details.label: Kathy’s essay
details.value: Victorian novels.
details.zh: Kathy 的 essay 主题是 Victorian novels，不是现代诗。

details.label: Book in the argument
details.value: Daniel Deronda, by George Eliot.
details.zh: 争执时 Kathy 正在读 George Eliot 的 Daniel Deronda。

details.label: Keffers
details.value: The grumpy man responsible for practical upkeep at the Cottages.
details.zh: Keffers 负责设施与杂务，并不是新的 guardian。

details.label: Veteran couple
details.value: Susie and Greg help Kathy notice television-derived mannerisms.
details.zh: Susie 与 Greg 的互动使 Kathy 看出部分“成熟表现”来自电视。
